title: Small-change safety checklist & quick followups
body:
TL;DR
Quick checklist and reviewer heuristics for small PRs (bugfixes, tiny refactors, feature flags flips). Keep this in your head for 1–3 file, <200 LOC, low-risk PRs. Use as a fast gating flow: if anything hits a red flag below, escalate to full PR checklist.

Context / intent
- Purpose: reduce post-merge rollbacks for small, high-frequency changes (config flips, guard clauses, tiny refactors).
- Typical examples: change default timeout, adjust backoff, rename param, remove a metric, small SQL predicate fix.
- Not for schema changes, migrations, infra, or perf-critical runtime loops.

Quick safety checklist (pass/fail, 1–2 min each)
1) Impact surface (pass if confined to single service or test files)
   - Files changed: are there client-facing APIs? If yes -> escalate.
2) Behavioral change (pass if change is pure refactor or small opt-in flag)
   - Is this altering behavior for existing users? (Y/N)
3) Data mutations (red flag)
   - Any writes to DB, SQS, metrics removal? If yes -> escalate + smoke tests.
4) Latency / hot path (red flag)
   - Touches tokenization/serving loop/critical path? If yes -> perf bench + SRE review.
5) Configs and defaults
   - If default changes, is there a feature flag? If not, add one or justify roll out plan.
6) Auth / permission boundaries (red flag)
   - Any check that could widen access? If yes -> security review.
7) Tests (must-have minimal)
   - Unit(s) covering changed logic + one terse integration/smoke that exercises the path.
8) Telemetry/observability (soft requirement)
   - Add a temporary metric/log line if behavior change is subtle. At minimum, add a DEBUG log.
9) Rollback path (mandatory)
   - Can this be reverted with a one-liner? (config flip, revert commit, flag off)

Lightweight reviewer heuristics
- Diff scan: focus on conditional logic, boundary checks, and 3rd-party call sites.
- Read tests: do tests express intent? If not, ask for an explicit one-liner test that demonstrates success case.
- PR description: must contain risk, rollout plan, and how to validate in prod (queries, dashboards).
- Commit hygiene: squash trivial WIP commits; keep single coherent change.

Local/CI quick tests to run before requesting review
- Unit tests: run the test file(s) impacted.
- Smoke: locally run the minimal flow (script below) or run the smoke job in CI: smoke-small-change.
- Dev env check: toggle the same feature flag locally to mimic prod default.

Example local smoke script (pseudo)
- export FEATURE_X=true
- ./tools/run-local --route /api/x --payload small.json
- tail -f logs/local | grep 'feature_x'

Rollout plan (1–2 lines)
- Canary: deploy to one zone/1% traffic for 15 minutes -> verify error rate and latency stable -> 10% for 1h -> ramp to 100% if green.
- If no rollout infra, keep feature flag OFF and coordinate a slow config flip during low-traffic window.

Rollback plan (1–2 lines)
- Preferred: flip feature flag OFF (instant).
- Fallback: revert commit and trigger CI redeploy. Document the revert steps in the PR description.

Common gotchas for small changes (things I keep tripping on)
- Hidden side-effects: helper functions modified in one place but used widely. Grep for callers.
- Metrics/alerts: removing metric names breaks dashboards -> add migration note.
- Cache invalidation: changing key format silently breaks caches.
- DB indices: small predicate changes can cause full table scans. Check explain plan for sensitive queries.

Follow-ups / TODOs after merge (short list)
- Add a short note to CHANGELOG.md if user-visible.
- If telemetry added: file a follow-up to remove DEBUG after 48–72h or promote to an actual metric.
- If test added: ensure test is not flaky and add to flakiness dashboard if flaky in next CI runs.

Reviewer templates (copy-paste into PR review)
- Quick pass checklist: Impact surface OK / Tests present / Rollback path OK / Observability present.
- If any NO: request changes and call out the specific missing item.

Notes to self (scratchy)
- Saved time when I required a smoke metric line for a weird config flip last week (PR #4791). That saved a rollback.
- For small SQL fixes: run EXPLAIN on staging; ask DB team if unsure.

Links & refs
- PR exemplar: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4791
- Team guideline: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Small+Change+Guidelines
- Incident ref: JIRA-CORE-897 (cfg flip rollback, Nov 2025)

Open questions / improvements to this doc
- Should we add an explicit flakiness check for added tests? (maybe a 3-run local flake check command)
- Can we produce a T-shirt sizing (S/M/L) to automatically choose reviewer depth?

End.
